note: Recast from the original description in Hagen 1858, Monographie der Termiten (Linnaea Entomologica 12, pp. 238—239), the original being a Latin diagnosis with a detailed German account. Hagen had only 1 incomplete specimen (no body, no hindwing), so only the alate is described; the specimen came from Cuba, collected by Poeppig and held in the Vienna museum. It was originally placed in Termes (Termes simplex) and is now referred to Prorhinotermes. Hagen points out especially that this species is exceptional within Termes in having no media at all.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Alate pale yellowish brown, sparsely hairy, the head and pronotum polished; legs and antennae paler, whitish yellow, the apices of the spurs and tarsal claws black. What is most peculiar about this species among the Termes known to Hagen is that the media of the wing is entirely absent; compound eyes round and large, strongly projecting, the oval ocelli closely applied to the inner margin of the compound eye; anterior margin of the antennal socket deeply concave, receiving the raised clypeus; pronotum 2 times as wide as long, with a depressed point in the middle of the anterior margin, the posterior margin narrow and upturned.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Pale yellowish brown, sparsely hairy, the head and pronotum polished; legs and antennae paler, whitish yellow, the apices of the spurs and tarsal claws black; wings water-clear, the two horny marginal veins yellow, the wing scales brownish. Head medium-sized, nearly circular, rather strongly convex, slightly narrowed anteriorly; compound eyes round, large, strongly projecting; ocelli oval, closely applied to the inner margin of the compound eye. Occiput semicircular; a shallow depression on the vertex, with a small fontanelle (an open round pore) in its middle, between the eyes. The concave anterior margin encloses the raised clypeus. Antenna incomplete (15 segments preserved), slightly longer than the head, thickening towards the apex; basal segment longer than wide, segment 2 as long as wide, segment 3 slightly shorter, all three cylindrical; the remaining segments gradually thickening, at first obcordate and then globular. Labrum narrower than the clypeus, as long as wide, rounded anteriorly. Maxillary palps slightly exceeding the mouth. Outer lobes of the labium very thin. Pronotum slightly narrower than the head, 2 times as wide as long, the anterior margin slightly concave, the anterior angles strongly rounded; the rounded sides pass in an arc into the posterior margin; pronotum fairly flat, the moderately depressed anterior angles slightly bent down; a depressed point in the middle of the anterior margin, the posterior margin narrow and upturned. Body missing. The only foreleg preserved is long and stout, the tibia with 2 spurs at its apex; the first 3 tarsal segments short, segment 4 nearly 2 times as long as the first three together; claw short, stout, nearly straight; no pulvillus. Wing 4 times as long as wide; wing scale large, longer than the pronotum, truncate, hardly curved on the outer side. Wing widening evenly from the base, the greatest width just before the elliptical apex. Subcosta close to the costa, curving round the apex almost to the posterior margin. Media entirely absent. Submedia running before the middle of the wing width, nearly straight, giving off 11 slightly curved, partly bifurcate branches to the posterior margin. The veins are very thick, and apart from the marginal area the whole wing membrane is coarsely scarred by numerous incomplete veins, which appear as recurrent, partly vertical cross-veins between the subcosta and the submedia. Hindwing missing. Head, margins of the pronotum and wing scales covered with fairly long hairs. Measurements: length with wings 10 mm, body length about 5 mm, wingspan 17 mm.
